course_name_original: Dirección y Gestión de Proyectos Multidisciplinares
prerequisites: Good capacity for comprehensive reading of texts in Spanish and English
Ability to search and identify bibliography
Ability to write reports in Spanish
Basic knowledge of projects, planning, and documentation acquired through undergraduate courses

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for the integration of technologies, applications, services, and systems typical of Computer Engineering, in a generalist manner, and in broader and multidisciplinary contexts.

Capacity for strategic planning, elaboration, direction, coordination, and technical and economic management in the fields of computer engineering related, among others, to: systems, applications, services, networks, IT infrastructures or facilities, and software development centers or factories, respecting the adequate fulfillment of quality and environmental criteria and in multidisciplinary work environments.

Capacity for the direction of research, development, and innovation projects, in companies and technology centers, guaranteeing the safety of people and property, the final quality of products, and their homologation.
Understand the most standardized processes and methodologies at an international level for project management.
Be able to carry out preliminary studies and technical-economic feasibility analysis of projects.
Be able to organize and direct work teams in multidisciplinary environments.
Know and manage techniques to define plans and programs according to the organization's strategy.
Be able to manage an organization's project portfolio.

syllabus_topics: Processes and methodologies for project management
Integral management of deadlines and costs
The commercial, social, and ethical context of projects
Preparation of a project management plan
Preparation of the exposition and defense of group work
teaching_methods: Individual activities on the Virtual Campus

assessment_methods.method: Group work, memory submission, exposition and oral defense
Final in-person knowledge test (multiple choice/short questions, application exercises)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, each of the three parts (group work, individual work, and in-person test) must be approved with a minimum score of 5 out of 10. The final grade for the ordinary session is calculated as: Final Grade = 0.6 x Group Work + 0.1 x Individual Work + 0.3 x In-person Test. Attending exposition and oral defense sessions for group work and at least 80% of practical sessions is mandatory for group work approval. For the extraordinary session, previously approved group and individual work will be considered; otherwise, a score of 0 will be assigned. A new in-person knowledge test must be passed with at least 5 out of 10. The final grade for the extraordinary session is: Final Grade = 0.6 x In-person Test + 0.4 x Work Grade (where Work Grade = 0.2 x Individual Work + 0.8 x Group Work). If no work was approved in the ordinary session, the maximum possible grade in the extraordinary session is 6 points. Differentiated evaluation follows the same criteria as the extraordinary session.
